q1_issues.issue: the direct object "the move" is given no role atom on the describe event — it appears only inside the sealed term — so the describing has no stated object and "what did the Commission describe?" binds nothing.
the parse takes the sealing route (complement sealed under Theme) but assigns the describer Agent, while the instruction set makes the holder Experiencer exactly when the complement seals.

(Inheritance executive_body executive) exposes a relational/classifying adjective that fails the predication test (*"the body is executive"), which the instruction set says is never exposed as a modifier genus.

q2_gaps: active object-complement "V NP as <predicate>" ("described the move as legally unwarranted..."): the instruction set covers finite that-clause attitudes, direct quotation and the impersonal "is considered to be" passive, but not this active construction, so neither the sealing decision nor the object's role is fixed

domain-adverb + adjective compounds ("legally unwarranted", "economically unfounded", "politically unhelpful") have no licensed decomposition — the parse fuses them into opaque symbols with no genus atom, and the compound-kind rules do not reach adverb+adjective pairs
notes: The appositive handling is right — no tense of its own, so the typing, the "powerful" property and the PartOf link all take the past host clause's wrapper — and the definite "the move" correctly projects its typing to top level out of the seal. Verbatim quotation loss is a registered limitation, not a defect.
